surveyContext.method: The report says local residents were interviewed about river use and fish/other aquatic animals caught. The catch table is based on local reports, not specimen-based fish sampling.
surveyContext.reportStatement: The source says five stations were reported by locals as sites of minor fishing activity and that catches were for domestic consumption. It reports 12 fish and other aquatic-animal categories across those stations.
surveyContext.samplingDateInterpretation: The February 2018 dates are freshwater ecology station-survey dates; the report does not provide taxon-specific capture dates.

limitations: The report frames the catch table as local interview reports; no fish voucher, specimen number, diagnostic image, taxon-specific collection date, catch count or standardized fish sampling method is supplied for these names.
The table mixes printed binomials with family/genus ranks, local names and broad animal groups; report wording such as 'crabs (ulang)' is retained without silently resolving the common-name conflict.
The field-station coordinates locate environmental survey stations only. They must not be mapped as exact fish observations or turned into river/creek geometry.
The statement that catches were used for domestic consumption is not food-safety evidence or a current advisory.
This is an old, project-specific and minor-fishing/interview snapshot across five stations, not a complete survey of Bulacan, Pampanga, the Pampanga Basin, or all seasons.
No item-specific reuse permission has been confirmed; no app projection or public table extraction is approved.
nextStep: Seek voucher-backed or independently reviewable recent fish surveys for the named Central Luzon rivers and reservoirs; keep this JICA interview-based, station-bounded catch context separate from verified specimens, current presence, food safety and legal fishing advice.
